title: GBX Professional Services, 30-second brand commercial
how_to_use: Paste `params` into OpenArt for the model and mode below (Seedance 2.5, text to video). The prompt is a full script: shot list with timings, voiceover lines, on-screen text, music and voice direction. Generate at 480p first to check pacing and the read, then re-run at 1080p. If the model shortens the read, cut the lines marked optional. Do not name a real actor in the prompt: describe the voice instead, as done here. The `alternate` block is the same spot set up for Wan 3.0.

params.prompt:
A 30-second cinematic brand commercial for GBX Professional Services, a Melbourne business consultancy. Single continuous piece, five beats, calm and premium, no rush.

VISUAL STYLE: editorial, understated, expensive. Dark charcoal and deep teal palette with warm off-white highlights, fine film grain, soft directional light, shallow depth of field, slow deliberate camera moves (slow push-ins, gentle lateral tracking, one slow tilt). Real-feeling Australian professionals in their thirties to fifties, diverse, natural and unposed, in a modern Melbourne office with the city skyline through the glass. No stock-photo smiles, no pointing at screens, no logos other than the GBX wordmark on the end card, no text on screen except the lines listed below.

VOICEOVER: one male voice throughout. Warm, unhurried, relaxed baritone, easy confidence, friendly and dry, a neutral accent that leans Australian, the kind of voice that sounds like a capable mate rather than an announcer. Conversational pacing with natural pauses. No shouting, no sales energy, no echo.

MUSIC AND SOUND: minimal. A low, slow ambient pad with a soft piano motif, a single warm swell under the final line, quiet room tone and subtle office ambience. Voice always clear above the music.

BEAT 1, 0 to 5 seconds. Dawn over the Melbourne skyline from a high office window, the city still quiet, light just arriving on the glass. Slow push in toward an empty desk with a closed notebook and a cup of coffee.
VOICEOVER: "Most businesses don't need more advice. They need a clearer picture."

BEAT 2, 5 to 12 seconds. Inside the office: a woman in her forties studies a clean dashboard on a monitor, teal charts, calm; cut to two colleagues walking a whiteboard process map; cut to a hand moving a single card along a pipeline board. Everything ordered, nothing frantic.
VOICEOVER: "GBX Professional Services helps firms run sharper. The numbers, the process, the pipeline, and AI that actually earns its keep."

BEAT 3, 12 to 19 seconds. A bright workplace training room. A relaxed presenter at the front, twenty staff of all ages listening, a slide behind them that reads only: Super, explained. A young employee nods as something clicks; an older colleague writes a note.
ON-SCREEN TEXT, small, lower third, off-white: Education, not advice.
VOICEOVER: "And we teach people about money. Plainly. At work, in language a whole team can follow."

BEAT 4, 19 to 25 seconds. A laptop on a kitchen bench at night, someone tapping through a simple one-question-per-screen tool on a website in the same charcoal and teal palette; a progress bar filling; a result card appearing. Cut to a handshake across a table in the office, easy and unhurried.
VOICEOVER: "Free tools before you ever hire us. A ten-day Diagnostic when you're ready."

BEAT 5, 25 to 30 seconds. Three leaders standing together at the office window, city behind them, not looking at the camera, talking easily. Slow tilt up to the skyline, then cut to a clean end card: charcoal background, the wordmark GBX in a light serif with PROFESSIONAL SERVICES in small spaced capitals beside it, a thin teal rule, and beneath it the line: Sharper businesses. Financially fluent people. Then, smaller: gbxps.com
VOICEOVER: "Three leaders. One operating view. Melbourne-based, working anywhere." (short pause) "GBX Professional Services."

All on-screen text must be spelled exactly as written. Hold the end card for the final two seconds with the music resolving.

voice_direction.summary: Neutral accent leaning Australian, warm relaxed baritone, easy confidence, friendly and a little dry, conversational pacing. Think capable mate, not announcer.
voice_direction.avoid: Do not name a real actor or public figure in the prompt. OpenArt models do not reproduce a specific person's voice or likeness, and a request to imitate one can be refused. Describing the qualities of the voice, as above, gets the same feel.

script_only: Most businesses don't need more advice. They need a clearer picture.

And we teach people about money. Plainly. At work, in language a whole team can follow.

optional_cuts_if_the_read_runs_long: Drop 'and AI that actually earns its keep.' from beat 2.

compliance.rule: No claim of financial advice. The education beat carries 'Education, not advice.' on screen and the voiceover says 'teach', never 'advise'.
compliance.review: Log the finished cut in docs/content-review-log.md before it is published anywhere.

alternate.note: Same script. Wan 3.0 renders 30 seconds in one pass at up to 1080p with an audio track; set mode to prime for the higher-fidelity tier. Prompt limit is 4500 characters, so use the condensed prompt below.
